title: An operator's measured clear closes a trouble and stays on its record
intention: cairn/devices/trouble's drain fold carries a clear emission's values['hand'] onto the cleared_by entry it appends (as 'hand'), and a clear whose measured hand class is an operator (akien or cc) closes the trouble even when the notified set names only the other operator, because Akien and CC are both operators; a hand of class gate or unknown still clears only as today (its 'by' must name a notified recipient).
why: Akien 2026-10-10: "to the best of your ability, get it all closed", pre-approved through PROVED. Measured 2026-10-11 by cc0 after Akien ran ~/.akien/temp/clear-who-writes-what.sh (commons 9306593): all 9 clears landed in the trouble records as cleared_by {by: 'akien'}, but (1) the commons .artifact-journal.jsonl records every one of those 9 'clear' writes with caller class 'gate', because the write happens in the trouble device's process at the drain (cairn/devices/trouble/shim.py _fold, CLEAR_GATE), not in the clearer's; so cairn/machines/counting_block/block.py:164-176, which teaches a row only when the clear's journal caller class is 'akien', taught NO row: a read-only block.compile(block.read_journals()) on 2026-10-11 returns increments [] and every who-writes-what clear in the journal as disposition cleared:gate, so no clear has taught a row since the block was armed; and (2) every one stays standing OPEN, because its notified set is ['cc'] (DEFAULT_RECIPIENTS) and trouble.py clear() closes only when every notified recipient has cleared. The clearer's hand is lost at the emission: cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py clear_trouble emits {by, what_changed} and nothing measured; 'by' is a self-declared word.
traces_to: Law 6 (the holder still decides; it now decides on a measured hand); Law 7 (the cleared_by entry keeps whose hand it was); Akien's 2026-10-11 operator spec.
how: cairn/devices/trouble only. shim.py _fold CLEAR_GATE branch: pass hand=values.get('hand') to self._device.clear. trouble.py clear(): new keyword hand: dict | None = None, stored on the appended cleared_by entry; OPERATORS = ('akien', 'cc') module tuple; after appending, if fold((hand or {}).get('class')) in OPERATORS the trouble is CLEARED (resolution = that entry); otherwise the existing outstanding-recipients rule. _handle_clear (bus) passes hand=None (a bus request carries no measured hand; that path stays as today). Add a bus verb 'clears' answering {'clears': [{'id', 'standing', 'by', 'hand_class', 'at'} for every cleared_by entry of every trouble whose id starts with body['prefix']]}, small by construction (no occurrences), for the counting block (0539e85f8b2d). Docstrings cite Akien 2026-10-11 verbatim.
falsifier: cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_an_operators_measured_clear_closes.py under PROVES {'1c1b18bac2eb': {'1','2','3'}} on a scratch trouble store and log root: (1) a trouble notified ['cc'], cleared through a clear emission whose hand.class is 'akien', is CLEARED after the drain and its cleared_by entry carries that hand; (2) the same with hand.class 'gate' and by 'akien' stays OPEN (today's rule); (3) the 'clears' verb with prefix 'who-writes-what-' answers one row per cleared_by entry with hand_class, and no occurrences key. Hollow: ignoring hand in clear() reds 1 and 3.

decisions.text: Akien 2026-10-11 (verbatim, /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/ideas/2026-10-11-ah-so-lets-review-the-original-trouble.json): 'tickets announce themselves to the operator, and because of how you and i work together, for that statement you and i are both operators.' So a measured operator hand closes the trouble whichever operator was notified; the notified set stays as who was TOLD. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
Only a MEASURED hand counts as an operator; the 'by' word alone never does, or any process could close any trouble by typing a name. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The 9 who-writes-what troubles Akien cleared on 2026-10-11 carry no hand (their emissions predate c2172127d7a4). They are not rewritten: they stay OPEN and close the next time Akien clears them with this built. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The trouble device declares a 'clears' verb: body {'prefix': str} (empty or absent = every trouble); it answers {'clears': [...]} with one row per cleared_by entry of each trouble whose id starts with the prefix, keys exactly {id, standing, by, hand_class, at}; hand_class is fold(hand['class']) or 'unknown' when the entry carries no hand. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
